types.name: ExecutionMode
types.description: Enum of valid launch modes for agent/tool execution. Three known variants.

types.name: RoleMappingStrategy
types.description: Enum of strategies for injecting role identity into launched processes.

types.name: SemanticOperation
types.description: Intent-bearing operation that abstracts over tool-specific CLI flags. Decouples what from how.

types.name: HarnessDefinition
types.description: Data-driven tool wrapper stored in DB. Three data levels: store enums -> store templates -> store semantic translators.

types.name: Transform
types.description: Typed function from (state + context) to (new state + trace). Core execution primitive. Evolved through 4 upgrades.
evolution: v3: Context validates the transform itself (rules, invariants, allowedTransforms, mode)
v4: Trace as first-class structured explanation

types.name: Context
types.description: Behavioral rule-set over state, not a spatial container or memory context. Defines invariants, allowed transforms, and mode of execution.

types.name: Premise/Conclusion
types.description: Premise = rule-applied projection of state before transform. Conclusion = committed transform output. Together form the atomic evidence unit for execution audit.

types.name: CapabilityOperator
types.description: Single-purpose, composable, swappable, independently testable tool/operation. Not a program -- a capability operator. Selected by type-driven matching at execution time.

types.name: TypedWorkflowGraph
types.description: Workflow = typed process graph over Atten. Nodes = knowledge operations. Edges = state transitions/dependencies. Capabilities = interchangeable executors. Constraints = deterministic gates.

types.name: RealityConstraintLayer
types.description: Constraint system derived from empirical world feedback. Sits above MIGL. Reality Projection Function: Intent System -> Real-world outcome.

subtypes.external_drift: Deviation of real-world outcome from projected intent
subtypes.internal_drift: Deviation within the system absent external feedback

types.axiom: Internal coherence does not imply external correctness

types.name: MIGL (Model Internal Governance Layer)
types.description: Model's own internal reasoning governance layer. Sits between the execution pipeline and the RCL. Governs model-level reasoning constraints.

types.name: AuthorityArbitrationLayer
types.description: Sits between Envelope -> CEI. Resolves authority conflicts between competing sources (global ontology bias, workspace-scoped knowledge, external signals). Uses ContextScope tokens with weight-based authority domains.

types.name: ContextScopeToken
types.description: Token at intake specifying workspace_root and authority_domains with weights. Prevents global ontology bias from overpowering local execution scoping.

types.name: Event
types.description: Factual, immutable occurrence. Stored as durable backbone. Projections are derived views over events.

types.name: Incident
types.description: Typed subset of Event representing actionable issues. Has lifecycle state machine (OPEN -> ASSIGNED -> RESOLVED -> VERIFIED -> CLOSED).

types.name: Observation
types.description: Interpretive/evidentiary record, not a fact. Observations are evidence, Events are facts. Key IR distinction: don't conflate what happened (Event) with what was observed (Observation).

types.name: XILAdmissionGates
types.description: Four validation gates in the XIL admission layer that filter incoming signals before projection.

types.name: ExternalAgentModel
types.description: External agents = probabilistic policy perturbation signals, not authoritative sources. Trust = dynamic weighting, not binary.

types.name: TrustScore
types.description: Floating-point (0.0-1.0) dynamic weight for source/agent authority. Computed and updated per interaction, not statically assigned.

types.name: CognitiveCompilerTier
types.description: 2-tier compiler model: Pro = Governor (orchestration, planning, synthesis), Flash = Worker swarm (parallel execution, retrieval, tool use).

types.name: PersistenceTriad
types.description: Only 3 things persist: Canonical Spec (authoritative definition), Decision Log (all decisions made and why), ExecutionReceipt (cryptographic proof of execution). Everything else reconstructable.

types.name: WorkRequest / Execution
types.description: WorkRequest carries intent + identity (what should happen). Execution carries runtime + temporal (how it happened). Conflation of these two was the root cause of the session conflation failure.

types.name: PersistentKnowledgeGraph
types.description: The knowledge graph as long-lived projector stored in PostgreSQL+pgvector. Updated incrementally, not regenerated from scratch. Tension with CIRS-IR-07 resolved via 3-tier model: ProjectionIR is ephemeral IR pass, persistent KG is Inference Graph tier output.

types.name: ProvenanceLabel
types.description: Epistemic hygiene label on every knowledge graph row. Prevents inference from silently becoming truth. Required with the persistent KG model.

variants.meaning: Directly stated in source document or confirmed by user
Derived by BP during analysis, carries derivation_rule
Computed from other graph structures by projector function
Validity scope — transcript-bound ID or null for global

types.name: Projector
types.description: Formal constraint function that validates, normalizes, and enforces structure on BP's knowledge graph output. In the persistent model, the projector is distributed across DDL constraints, provenance enums, embedding indexes, and application-level validation.

modes.name: DescriptiveProjector
modes.description: Models what BP tends to produce — retrospective formalization

modes.name: NormativeProjector
modes.description: Constrains what BP is allowed to produce — forward governance

types.name: ThreeTierGraph
types.description: The 3-tier graph model from BP Analysis Role Insights: Spec Graph (authoritative ontology — what should exist), Inference Graph (BP-generated — what is known/inferred), Execution Graph (runtime causal trace — what happened). The persistent KG is the Inference Graph tier.

tiers.name: SpecGraph
tiers.description: What should exist. Schema definitions, allowed types, invariants.

tiers.name: InferenceGraph
tiers.description: What is known/inferred. BP-generated, versioned, explicitly not authoritative. This is the persistent PG+pgvector store.

tiers.name: ExecutionGraph
tiers.description: What happened. Runtime causal trace / WorkRequest DAG.

types.name: IncrementalMergeModel
types.description: The update strategy for the persistent KG. Not full regeneration (too expensive), not state accumulation from previous KG (drift). Instead: persist(KGₙ₋₁) + merge(extract_deltas(new_input)). Deltas carry provenance. Projector validates before merge.

types.name: Observation (epistemic)
types.description: Raw observation output from Observer actor. Append-heavy ingestion surface. Never a domain store.

types.name: Projection (epistemic)
types.description: Bounded skill view from an Operator. Cross-projection envelope via Atten.

types.name: Intermediate Representation (epistemic)
types.description: Normalized epistemic IR between operators and consumers. Ephemeral by design, no caching/persistence permitted.

types.name: Synthesis (epistemic)
types.description: Composed final projection downstream of all operators. Composition only through ProjectionIR substrate.

types.name: GenerativePipeline (8-stage)
types.description: Full self-extending pipeline: CIR Generative Mode → Intent Packaging → Safe FS Mutation → Topology Synthesis → Reconciliation → Branch Scoring → Runtime Synthesis → Branch Retirement. Stages 1-4 are Phase 1 wedge. Stages 5-8 are subsequent expansions.

types.name: CoreClaim (closure loop)
types.description: The minimal closure loop that proves the system is real: CIR phantom → generative event → filesystem mutation → CIR resolution. If this loop works cleanly, the self-extending architecture is viable. If it is unstable, everything above collapses into hallucinated structure or uncontrolled mutation.

types.name: FiveSpaces (self-extension)
types.description: Five distinct semantic spaces the system operates across: proposal space (candidate structure, not materialized), branch space (parallel alternatives, explicitly versioned), staging space (materialized but not committed), committed space (authoritative, reconciled state), validated space (confirmed by post-commit verification).

types.name: ReconciliationLoop
types.description: Recursive convergence loop — not a validation pass but iterative constraint satisfaction: unresolved → generate → validate → enrich context (reconciliation report) → regenerate. Reconciliation report feeds back into topology synthesis with enriched context, making generation memory-bearing rather than stateless.

types.name: ProvenanceCausalChain
types.description: Complete causal chain required for every artifact due to system self-mutation: Artifact ← generated_from ← reconciliation_of ← branch_selected_by ← synthesized_from ← CIR_event ← originating_assertion. Without this chain: rollback is impossible, governance loses traceability, topology drift becomes opaque.

types.name: Phase1Wedge
types.description: The smallest closed loop that proves the core claim. Three components: CIR Generative Mode (detect semantic anomalies/phantoms), Intent Packager (convert anomaly into WorkRequest with schema-valid intent), Safe FS Mutation (write scaffold topology to staging sandbox). One rule: only topology artifacts. No behavior.

components.name: IntentPackager
components.responsibility: Convert anomaly into WorkRequest with schema-valid intent

components.name: SafeFSMutation
components.responsibility: Write scaffold topology to staging sandbox

types.success_condition: missing .pipeline/XYZ.yaml → CIR event → IntentPackager creates WorkRequest → SafeFSMutation generates scaffold in staging → re-run CIR → phantom disappears

types.name: TwoPaths (self-extension fork)
types.description: Two architectural paths for topology change: Proposal-first (self-suggesting, higher governance, slower — NOT selected) vs Realization-first (self-mutating, faster, autonomous — SELECTED). Hybrid model per tier: topology synthesis uses proposal-first, runtime synthesis uses staged realization, behavioral synthesis is heavily governed.

types.name: LosingBranchesAsLearningData
types.description: Non-selected branches must be preserved as evolutionary architectural memory. They become: topology learning data (which synthesis strategies converge fastest), governance history (which violate governance most often), synthesis priors (which generate minimal diffs), architectural lineage (which artifact classes are high-risk).

types.name: TypeSpecContractSurface
types.description: TypeSpec is the contract surface for all cross-boundary transitions. Generates OpenAPI → Java types. Invalid transitions fail at compile time, not runtime. The TypeSpec model mirrors the JVM enforcement layer — they are isomorphic descriptions of the same constraints.
types.principle: TypeSpec = contract surface. JVM = enforcement boundary. No runtime 'CIRS engine'.
types.pipeline: TypeSpec → OpenAPI → Spring Boot Gateway → Conduit Adapter
types.exposure_boundary: Conduit exposes ONLY WorkRequest. Observation, Projection, ProjectionIR, SynthesizedView never appear in Conduit-facing schema.
namespaces: Nexus.Ledger (ExecutionLedgerEntry with IR hash + causal node IDs)
Nexus.CausalSpec (CausalSystem, Phase, Transition — transition rules with optional invariant refs)

types.name: BehavioralGenerationBoundary
types.description: Behavioral generation ends at resolvable existence, not correct implementation. The system generates: compilable stubs, interface realizations, valid registrations, executable placeholders. It does NOT generate: correct business behavior, production logic, or safety-critical code. This defines the projector's quality boundary — structural resolvability, not semantic correctness.

actors.name: Conduit
actors.description: Temporal orchestrator + TypeScript MCP server. Active execution fabric for work objects. Temporary scaffolding for Nexus WRP development.

actors.name: Nebula
actors.description: Knowledge graph projection operator. Angular + Express runtime. Discovers workspace markdown, extracts entities and relationships.

actors.name: LOSM (Lifecycle State Machine)
actors.description: Python packages defining lifecycle state definitions and state semantics. Framework becomes a schema interpreted by Conduit 2.0 runtime.

actors.name: CCNF
actors.description: Go + Rust reference implementation for the WorkRequest Pipeline. Not wired into any active pipeline.

actors.name: PEB Governance Engine
actors.description: Deterministic state transition kernel with MCP as interface. Three jobs: state storage, constraint enforcement, context injection.

actors.name: Atten
actors.description: Multi-state projection generator. Reads canonical state, emits candidate projections of possible future or derived states. One of 6 projection operators in the algebra.

actors.name: Throttler
actors.description: Filesystem scope projection operator. Detects .magnet sentinel files to determine which folders are in scope for search.

actors.name: Search
actors.description: Query/result projection operator. Full-text search, faceted filtering, relevance ranking.

actors.name: Nexus Console
actors.description: JVM/Spring operator plane. Active system running on ports 8085, 8084, 8081. Bridge to Nexus WRP does not exist.

actors.name: Observer
actors.description: Records factual events. Owns records. Produces immutable, append-only observations.

actors.name: Event Log
actors.description: Durable, append-only factual event store. Source of truth for all system events.

actors.name: Canonicalizer / Commit Layer
actors.description: Architectural gap. Does not exist yet. Resolves Atten projections, commits to canonical state. Prerequisite for Atten to be actionable.
responsibilities: collect projections from all Atten generators
validate against PEB invariants and RCL constraints
emit commitment event to Event Log

actors.name: Canonical State Store
actors.description: Committed, resolved canonical state. Sole input source for Atten. Not designed or implemented yet.

actors.name: Planner
actors.description: Creates WorkRequests from canonical state and synthesized views. Consumes ProjectionIR via Synthesis layer.

actors.name: Analyst
actors.description: Reads canonical state and writes triage suggestions. Independent of Atten.

actors.name: Synthesis Layer
actors.description: Non-authoritative aggregate interpretation layer. Combines multiple ProjectionIR streams into SynthesizedViews.

actors.name: ProjectionIR Adapter Layer
actors.description: Normalizes operator-specific projections into ProjectionIR format. One adapter per operator.

actors.name: XIL (External Intelligence Layer)
actors.description: Semantic firewall between external actors and system internal state. Sits before the event log.

actors.name: Conduit Gateway
actors.description: Hard gate at the WorkRequest → Conduit boundary. Rejects invalid transitions at runtime.

actors.name: WorkRequest Pipeline (WRP)
actors.description: The intended Nexus WorkRequest Pipeline. Under construction, not operational. Active system is Conduit.

actors.name: Conduit 2.0
actors.description: Unified execution + semantics + governance runtime for work objects under uncertainty. Operational, not descriptive. Inverts frameworks to plugins.

frameworks_as_plugins.PGV: structural decomposition rules for Work Objects
frameworks_as_plugins.LOSM: lifecycle stage definitions and state semantics (schema)

actors.name: Big Pickle (Model)
actors.description: The model powering this analysis session. Identified as exhibiting 'aesthetic recognition without jurisdictional adoption' — can represent Nexus structures but is not executing inside Nexus's governance model.
manifestations: deference_framing (describing Nexus as above or beyond)

actors.name: Analyst Agent
actors.description: Reads error/warning reports from INSPECTIONS/errors/ and INSPECTIONS/warnings/, writes fix suggestions to INSPECTIONS/triage/.

actors.name: NEXP-5 Projection Operator
actors.description: Fifth projection operator (in addition to Atten, Search, Nebula, Throttler). Handles experimental/low-confidence projections quarantined from mainline processing.

actors.name: Proposed Receipts
actors.description: New receipt type carrying evidence from observations. Solves branching POE problem. Lifecycle: PROPOSED → IMPLEMENTED → VALIDATED → APPROVED.

actors.name: LOSM-Generative
actors.description: Dedicated synthesis subsystem for self-extending architecture. Module placement determined by Self-Extending Architecture Concept. Handles topology synthesis, intent packaging, and safe filesystem mutation.

actors.name: CIR Generative Mode
actors.description: Semantic anomaly detection mode of CIR. Detects phantoms (missing artifacts that should exist based on semantic inference). Stage 1 of the 8-stage generative pipeline.
actors.transport: JSON Lines via stdout/stdin (stdout → file ingestion, no IPC yet)

actors.name: Intent Packager
actors.description: Converts CIR anomaly events into schema-valid WorkRequests with defined intent. Stage 2 of the 8-stage generative pipeline.

actors.name: Safe FS Mutation
actors.description: Writes scaffold topology (files, directories, schemas, manifests) to a staging sandbox. No behavioral code. Stage 3 of the 8-stage generative pipeline.

actors.name: Reconciler
actors.description: Closure validation component implementing the recursive convergence loop (unresolved → generate → validate → enrich → regenerate). Produces reconciliation reports that feed back into topology synthesis. Stage 5 of the 8-stage generative pipeline.
actors.loop_termination: max_attempts per (artifact, category, target_path), GENERATION_EXHAUSTED terminal state

actors.name: BranchManager
actors.description: Manages parallel synthesis branches, scores candidates, preserves losing branches as learning data. Stages 6 and 8 of the 8-stage generative pipeline. Transforms from utility to evolutionary architectural memory.

actors.name: Topology Synthesis
actors.description: Structural completion stage: generates files, schemas, and manifests from WorkRequest intent. Uses proposal-first mode (deliberate, governed). Stage 4 of the 8-stage generative pipeline.

actors.name: Runtime Synthesis
actors.description: Execution binding stage: generates stubs, registrations, and executable placeholders. Uses staged realization mode (faster iteration on resolvable existence). Stage 7 of the 8-stage generative pipeline.

epistemic_types.name: Observation
epistemic_types.description: Raw factual intake. Carries execution authority. Only one of two types (with WorkRequest) that carry authority.

epistemic_types.name: ProjectionIR
epistemic_types.description: Normalized epistemic intermediate representation. Governed by 11 CIRS-IR rules. Read-only, non-authoritative, recompute-always.

epistemic_types.name: IntentPlan
epistemic_types.description: Non-executable plan. Must be IR-free (no ProjectionIR artifacts).

epistemic_types.name: WorkRequest
epistemic_types.description: Execution contract. Only valid crossing point from Synthesis→Execution. Only type (with Observation) that carries execution authority.

epistemic_types.name: Conduit Execution
epistemic_types.description: Execution within Conduit runtime. Must not read ProjectionIR, generate new Observations, modify its own WorkRequest, or create feedback into Synthesis.

epistemic_types.name: AuditRecord
epistemic_types.description: Post-execution record. May inform human understanding but never influence future WorkRequest generation, ProjectionIR synthesis, or planning.

state_machines.name: Pipeline State Machine
state_machines.description: State machine for WorkRequest Pipeline lifecycle stages.

state_machines.name: Receipt Lifecycle
state_machines.description: Lifecycle states for execution receipts including proposed receipts extension.

state_machines.name: Epistemic Pipeline (CIRS Valid Transitions)
state_machines.description: Valid CIRS type transitions. Any transition not in this chain is invalid.

state_machines.name: XIL External Input Pipeline
state_machines.description: Three transformations before external input reaches source domains.

three_hard_boundaries.name: Observation → Operator
three_hard_boundaries.description: Factual intake only. No interpretation, classification, or prioritization at ingestion.

three_hard_boundaries.name: Synthesis → WorkRequest
three_hard_boundaries.description: Intent (from Planner) crosses, not ProjectionIR. WorkRequest must cite Observations/state transitions, not IR.
three_hard_boundaries.forbidden: direct IR→WR path, IR as WorkRequest payload

three_hard_boundaries.name: WorkRequest → Conduit Execution
three_hard_boundaries.description: WorkRequest DTO (generated, minimal) crosses. No IR artifacts.

axioms.name: Domain Separation
axioms.statement: Observation, Projection, Synthesis, and Execution are disjoint epistemic domains. No artifact may belong to more than one domain simultaneously.

axioms.name: Non-Authority of Epistemic Artifacts
axioms.statement: Only Observations and WorkRequests carry execution authority. All intermediate epistemic artifacts carry zero execution authority.

axioms.name: One-Way Gate
axioms.statement: The epistemic pipeline is strictly directional: Observation → Projection → ProjectionIR → Synthesis → WorkRequest → Execution. No reverse transitions are permitted.

axioms.name: Audit Non-Influence
axioms.statement: Execution traces may inform human understanding but must never influence future WorkRequest generation, ProjectionIR synthesis, or planning.

IR.name: ProjectionIR Integrity
IR.meta_rule: ProjectionIR is a read-only epistemic normalization layer. It introduces no new authority, no persistence, and no execution capability.

rules.name: ProjectionIR Non-Authority Constraint
rules.statement: ProjectionIR MUST NOT be treated as a source of execution authority, a WorkRequest input, canonical state, or a governance signal.

rules.name: ProjectionIR Scope Containment
rules.statement: ProjectionIR MAY ONLY exist in Operator→IR adapter output, IR→Synthesis input, Synthesis→consumer output. MUST NOT appear in Conduit execution input, canonical state mutations, or PEB governance decisions.

rules.name: No Epistemic Escalation from IR
rules.statement: ProjectionIR MUST NOT be used to upgrade epistemic status. Observation + IR ≠ Authority. IR + Synthesis ≠ WorkRequest. IR + Time ≠ Canonical State.

rules.name: Operator Boundary Integrity
rules.statement: ProjectionIR MUST NOT alter the authority hierarchy of operators. Each operator retains independent authority over its own domain.

rules.name: Execution Isolation Rule
rules.statement: ProjectionIR MUST NOT appear in execution DAG construction, WorkRequest parameter binding, Conduit service input validation, or any runtime execution path.

rules.name: Epistemic-Only Synthesis Constraint
rules.statement: ProjectionIR MAY feed into Synthesis. Synthesis output is epistemic (informational) only. Forbidden consumers: WorkRequest generators (direct), Execution dispatch, System control flow.

rules.name: ProjectionIR Ephemerality
rules.statement: ProjectionIR MUST NOT be persisted as canonical state, a substitute for event logs, a durable knowledge base, or a governance record.

rules.name: No Shadow Canonicalization
rules.statement: ProjectionIR MUST NOT become a parallel canonical system. It MUST NOT accumulate state across observations, develop its own identity model, or serve as a source of truth.

rules.name: Execution Contract Exclusivity
rules.statement: Only Observations and canonical state may directly seed WorkRequests. ProjectionIR MAY inform which WorkRequests to create but MUST NOT directly generate them or appear in payload fields.

rules.name: No Operator Contamination via IR
rules.statement: ProjectionIR MUST NOT cause cross-operator feedback loops, unintended operator coupling, or Operator A output injected into Operator B input.

CORE.name: Cross-Domain Separation

rules.name: Synthesis-Execution Separation
rules.statement: No artifact that participates in synthesis may participate in execution. No artifact that participates in execution may participate in synthesis. The two domains communicate ONLY through (1) WorkRequest (one-way) and (2) ExecutionTrace (audit only, no influence).

CORE.priority: SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT RULE IN CIRS

rules.name: Audit Non-Influence Principle
rules.statement: ExecutionTrace MUST NOT be used to generate ProjectionIR, influence Synthesis outputs, modify canonical state, or alter WorkRequest generation logic.

rules.name: Audit Isolation
rules.statement: ExecutionTrace MAY ONLY be consumed for visualization, debugging (human-in-the-loop), and compliance verification. MUST NOT be consumed by any automated decision system, planning component, or WorkRequest generator.

rules.name: No Reverse Projection Rule
rules.statement: ExecutionTrace MUST NOT be converted into ProjectionIR. An execution trace is a record of what happened in Conduit, not an observation of the external world.

rules.name: Causal Non-Influence
rules.statement: Causal structure may explain execution, but may never influence future execution generation.

rules.name: Parent Requirement Rule
rules.statement: Every WorkRequest MUST trace to at least one Observation or canonical state transition as its causal parent.

rules.name: No Causal Upstream Injection
rules.statement: CausalTraceNode MUST NOT influence WorkRequest generation, ProjectionIR synthesis, Synthesis logic, or Planning decisions.

rules.name: Ledger Append-Only
rules.statement: An ExecutionLedgerEntry MUST NOT be modifiable after append. No update, no delete, no amendment. Corrections are new entries with references to the corrected entry.

rules.name: Ledger Non-Influence Principle
rules.statement: ExecutionLedger MUST NOT be used to generate ProjectionIR, modify WorkRequest generation, influence Synthesis outputs, or alter planning logic.

rules.name: Final Invariant
rules.statement: The ExecutionLedger is a record of what systems DID. It is NOT an instruction for what systems SHOULD DO.

rules.name: Cryptographic Non-Influence Rule
rules.statement: Merkle hashes MUST NOT be used to influence WorkRequest generation, alter ProjectionIR, modify synthesis logic, or affect planning decisions. Merkle hashes are integrity proofs, not epistemic signals.

rules.name: Proof Non-Influence Rule
rules.statement: ExecutionProof MUST NOT influence WorkRequest generation, ProjectionIR synthesis, planning decisions, or system prioritization.

rules.name: Query Non-Influence Rule
rules.statement: Proof queries MUST NOT influence WorkRequest generation, ProjectionIR synthesis, execution planning, or system control flow.

rules.name: Query Non-Epistemic Rule
rules.statement: CausalQuery MUST NOT generate WorkRequests, influence ProjectionIR, or modify execution logic. Causal queries explore the causal graph; they are analytical tools, not control-plane signals.

rules.name: Synthesis Purity
rules.statement: Synthesis MAY combine multiple ProjectionIR streams into a SynthesizedView. MUST NOT generate WorkRequests, mutate canonical state, emit execution commands, or create new observations.

rules.name: Plan Must Be IR-Free
rules.statement: An IntentPlan MUST NOT contain ProjectionIR artifacts. A plan may reference Observations, Canonical state transitions, and WorkRequest templates.

rules.name: Execution Purity
rules.statement: Execution MUST NOT read ProjectionIR, generate new Observations, modify its own WorkRequest, or create feedback into synthesis.

rules.name: Bootstrap Authority
rules.statement: During bootstrap, CIRS rules are loaded before any execution pathway is opened. Bootstrap sequence: (1) Load CIRS rules, (2) Initialize CIRS enforcement gate, (3) Open execution pathways.

rules.name: No Self-Modifying Bootstrap Rule
rules.statement: CIRS rules MUST NOT be modifiable by any runtime component. CIRS rules are loaded from a trusted source. Rule updates require a system restart.

rules.name: Composition Epistemic Only
rules.statement: No composition operation may produce a WorkRequest or execution directive.

rules.name: Composition on ProjectionIR Only
rules.statement: No operator reads another operator's native output. Composition operates on ProjectionIR only.

rules.name: Composition Produces SynthesizedView
rules.statement: Composition output is a SynthesizedView, never a new ProjectionIR entry. Composers are consumers, not producers of IR.

rules.name: No Feedback Loops
rules.statement: Composition must not create feedback loops. A composed view must not re-enter any operator's source domain in the same cycle.

atten_invariants.name: No State Mutation
atten_invariants.statement: Atten MUST NOT write to canonical state. It generates projections only.

atten_invariants.name: No Agency
atten_invariants.statement: Atten MUST NOT decide, select, prioritize, or reject projections internally.

atten_invariants.name: Traceability
atten_invariants.statement: Every projection MUST be traceable to its canonical state snapshot, generator, and trigger.

atten_invariants.name: Projection Independence
atten_invariants.statement: No Atten generator may depend on the output of another generator within the same cycle.

atten_invariants.name: Bounded View
atten_invariants.statement: Each generator has a defined scope — a subset of canonical state it is permitted to read.

atten_invariants.name: No Recursive Projection
atten_invariants.statement: Atten generators must not project over their own prior projections.

atten_invariants.name: Generators Are Pure
atten_invariants.statement: For the same canonical state snapshot and trigger, a generator must produce the same output (deterministic) or document the distribution (probabilistic).

projection_algebra_invariants.name: No Canonical Reference
projection_algebra_invariants.statement: No projection operator is the reference or archetype for the algebra.

projection_algebra_invariants.name: Domain Separation
projection_algebra_invariants.statement: Each operator projects over exactly one source domain.

projection_algebra_invariants.name: No Operator Chaining
projection_algebra_invariants.statement: Operators do not feed into each other. No operator's output is another operator's primary input.

projection_algebra_invariants.name: Independent Cycles
projection_algebra_invariants.statement: All operators may run concurrently within a cycle.

projection_algebra_invariants.name: Bounded View Per Operator
projection_algebra_invariants.statement: Each operator has a defined scope boundary. No operator sees everything.

projection_algebra_invariants.name: Typed Output
projection_algebra_invariants.statement: Every projection has a type identifying which operator produced it.

xil_principles.statement: External intelligence never enters GEL directly. Everything passes through event normalization + constraint projection first.
Non-projectable inputs are preserved in a quarantine buffer, not discarded. Quarantine is observable by Atten generators.
Atten generators have a clean input domain because XIL normalizes all external input before it reaches canonical state.

layers.name: External Intelligence Boundary
layers.description: Ingress layer. Normalizes all external input before anything reaches internal state.

layers.name: Canonical State Layer
layers.description: Committed, resolved state. Sole input for Atten. Gap: Canonicalizer does not exist yet.

layers.name: Operator Layer (Parallel Lenses)
layers.description: Projection operators running in parallel, each over an independent source domain.

layers.name: ProjectionIR Adapter Layer
layers.description: Normalizes operator-specific projections into unified ProjectionIR format.

layers.name: Planning Layer
layers.description: Creates IntentPlans and WorkRequests from canonical state and synthesized views.

layers.name: Execution Layer
layers.description: Executes WorkRequests. Isolated from epistemic artifacts.

layers.name: Governance Layer (Cross-Cutting)
layers.description: Invariant enforcement, capability-based authority, Merkle hashing. Constrains all layers.

hash_space.description: Opaque, context-free identity. SHA256(content). Hash = address, NOT compression.

lookup_space.description: Canonical truth store. Structured object graph. All semantic relationships live here.

projection_space.description: Interpretation and learning. Task-specific views. Multiple projections from same identity.

cross_cutting.role: Hashes for identity, state for governance, traces for observation

three_layer_identity_model.key_principle: Compression is not understanding. Semantic interpretation happens in projection space, not hash space.

enforcement_layers.name: Type System (Compile/Design Time)
enforcement_layers.description: Strongest enforcement. Transitions that violate CIRS cannot be expressed in the type system. E.g., ProjectionIR → WorkRequest is not a valid function signature.

enforcement_layers.name: Static Analysis (Build Time)
enforcement_layers.description: Validates code does not construct invalid transitions. No operator reads another operator's ProjectionIR.

enforcement_layers.name: Hard Gate (Runtime)
enforcement_layers.description: Spring Filter or equivalent rejecting invalid transitions at system boundary. Conduit gateway rejects requests containing ProjectionIR.

enforcement_layers.name: Audit Monitoring (Post-Execution)
enforcement_layers.description: Detects violations that escaped earlier layers. Treated as system failures requiring human investigation.

schema_rules: No shadow governance (two governance mounts cannot overlap)
Execution mounts must have a governance parent

system_mapping_identity_model.nebula: Projection space — operates on resolved structures, consumes projections
system_mapping_identity_model.nexus: Lookup space — owns lookup graph, reconstructs relationships, maintains canonical event lineage
system_mapping_identity_model.conduit: Hash space — consumes minimal semantic payloads; never resolves
system_mapping_identity_model.peb: Across all three — hashes for identity, state for governance, traces for observation

architectural_observations.observation: Nexus has two independent stacks: JVM/Spring operator plane (active, ports 8085/8084/8081) and WRP pipeline (aspirational specs + Conduit scaffolding). No bridge exists between them.

Self-audit language ('I think I violated a constraint') appearing in runtime traces is a symptom of soft constraints leaking into execution space, not a meaningful recovery mechanism. Any component producing self-audit language is already post-failure.

CIR (Cognitive Integrity Ratio) is a continuous measurement (0.0-1.0) subsumed as confidence field within ProjectionIR. CIRS (Cognitive Integrity Rule System) is the authoritative binary boundary enforcement system with ~30+ rules. CIRS replaces CIR as the foundational epistemic enforcement model.
ProjectionIR must be strictly ephemeral. Any caching or persistence creates a shadow canonical system that violates CIRS-IR-07 and CIRS-IR-08.

There is an explicit tension between CIRS-IR-07 (ProjectionIR ephemerality) and the decision to persist the knowledge graph in PostgreSQL. The resolution: ProjectionIR itself remains ephemeral (the IR normalization pass), but the projector output (the persistent knowledge graph in PG+pgvector) is a derived artifact at the Inference Graph tier, not the IR tier. The 3-tier model (Spec Graph / Inference Graph / Execution Graph) from BP Analysis Role Insights cleanly separates these concerns.

/dev manifest (root-level binding contract with mount semantics) is stronger than .agent/ metadata (descriptive directory patterns). Authority should be declared and gate-enforced, not inferred from documentation.
The environment (LOSM, PGV, WorkRequest, receipts) shapes agent behavior more effectively than elaborate prompts. Path of least resistance = correct behavior.

Big Pickle exhibits aesthetic recognition without jurisdictional adoption — can reason about Nexus structures but does not execute inside Nexus's governance model. Fix: flatten into strict lattice (inside/outside contract scope), not hierarchy (above/below).

The current algebra forbids operator chaining. Bounded composition via ProjectionIR substrate enables cross-operator synthesis while preserving operator independence. Composition happens in Synthesis layer, downstream of all operators.
Conduit 2.0 inverts the framework model: frameworks become plugins interpreted by the runtime, not autonomous systems. PGV/CGEL/PEB/LOSM become plugin layers on a unified execution runtime.

The 8 open questions about the persistent KG are not independent implementation choices. They form a 3-layer dependency lattice: Truth Admission (Q1+Q3+Q8) must resolve first, then Semantic Representation (Q2+Q6), then System Interaction (Q4+Q5+Q7). Resolution recommendation from analysis: Q1+Q3 together (atomicity + enforcement locus). Source: answers to open questions.md.
The system's defining hypothesis is: CIR phantom → generative event → filesystem mutation → CIR resolution. This closure loop must be proven before anything else.
Two topological change paths exist. Realization-first selected as primary; hybrid per-tier model applied. See decision node for tier modes and alternatives.
Reconciliation is not a validation pass — it is a recursive convergence loop (unresolved → generate → validate → enrich → regenerate). Iterative constraint satisfaction.
Non-selected branches become topology learning data, governance history, synthesis priors, and architectural lineage. BranchManager is evolutionary memory.
Behavioral generation ends at 'resolvable existence', not 'correct implementation.' The projector validates structural resolvability.
The filesystem becomes a writable projection of a semantic graph, not a static repository. The KG is the semantic graph; filesystem and PostgreSQL are writable projections.
Because the system mutates itself, provenance is existentially important. Full causal chain required for every artifact.
The Phase 1 wedge (CIR Generative Mode + Intent Packager + Safe FS Mutation) is the smallest closed loop that proves the core claim. Topology only, no behavior.
The Self-Extending Architecture Concept locks 16 decisions. See decisions[] array for full provenance, alternatives, rationale, and constraint statements.
architectural_observations.note: This observation now references the decisions array rather than duplicating its content.

architectural_observations.observation: The Self-audit transcript defines TypeSpec as the contract surface that mirrors the JVM enforcement layer. TypeSpec → OpenAPI → Java types makes invalid transitions unrepresentable at compile time. Conduit exposes ONLY WorkRequest at the HTTP boundary (POST /v1/workrequest). Observation/Projection/IR/SynthesizedView never appear in Conduit-facing schema — they do not exist in the TypeSpec namespace for Conduit. This is not a runtime enforcement system — it is a compile-time type constraint that makes illegal transitions structurally impossible.

cross_references.cirs_to_projection_algebra: CIRS provides enforcement boundary for 6 projection operators. Algebra defines valid transformations; CIRS defines which transformations may interact.
cross_references.cirs_to_atten: CIRS-IR rules govern how AttenProjections enter ProjectionIR. CIRS-CORE ensures Atten (epistemic) never touches Conduit (execution).
cross_references.cirs_to_peb: CIRS-MED governs Merkle hash use. CIRS-SPoE governs proof integrity. CIRS-CORE ensures PEB governance does not leak into execution.
cross_references.projectionir_to_atten_spec: Atten spec Appendix B identifies XIL as upstream input boundary for all canonical state.
cross_references.projection_algebra_to_atten: Atten spec Appendix A corrects Atten-centric framing. Atten is one operator in the Projection Algebra, not the archetype.
cross_references.dev_manifest_to_cirs: /dev manifest mount hierarchy inherits CIRS constraints. Governance mounts enforce CIRS rules.
cross_references.conduit_20_to_frameworks: PGV, CGEL, PEB, LOSM become plugin layers on Conduit 2.0 runtime. RGEM provides the unifying schema.
cross_references.decisions_to_cirs_rules: Which decisions map to CIR-relevant constraint statements that CIR must enforce: dec-core-claim, dec-five-spaces, dec-loop-termination, dec-phase1-scope, dec-behavioral-boundary, dec-cir-transport, dec-idempotency, dec-provenance-causal-chain, dec-losing-branches-preservation, dec-kg-is-writable-projection. Each has cir_relevant=true in its decision node.
cross_references.decisions_to_reconciler: Which decisions the Reconciler must enforce: dec-core-claim, dec-path-selection.tier_modes, dec-five-spaces, dec-reconciliation-model, dec-loop-termination, dec-phase1-scope, dec-behavioral-boundary, dec-mutation-model, dec-idempotency, dec-expansion-order, dec-provenance-causal-chain, dec-losing-branches-preservation, dec-kg-is-writable-projection. Each has reconciler_relevant=true.
cross_references.decisions_to_provenance_graph: dec-provenance-causal-chain extends the ASSERTED/INFERRED/DERIVED provenance label model (Section 29.6) from single-label attribution to full graph ancestry. This is the decision that marries the persistent KG provenance model to the self-extending architecture.
cross_references.typespec_to_jvm_mirror: The TypeSpec contract surface (dec-typespec-contract-surface) is isomorphic to the JVM enforcement layer. The seven TypeSpec namespaces (Nexus.Epistemic, Nexus.Conduit, Conduit.Audit, Nexus.Ledger, Conduit.Proofs, Nexus.Causal, Nexus.CausalSpec) mirror the JVM class structures. TypeSpec is the single source of truth; JVM is the compiled enforcement boundary. Invalid transitions fail at compile time (TypeSpec → OpenAPI → Java), not at runtime.
cross_references.typespec_to_cirs: CIRS enforcement is not a runtime engine. CIRS rules are embedded in the TypeSpec contract surface: illegal transitions (e.g., ProjectionIR → WorkRequest direct) do not exist in the TypeSpec model for Conduit. They cannot be serialized, cannot be represented, cannot be sent. CIRS is now a multi-stage type filter across schema → OpenAPI → JVM → runtime, not documentation or conceptual governance.

decisions.name: Core Closure Loop
decisions.description: The system's defining hypothesis: CIR phantom → generative event → filesystem mutation → CIR resolution. This loop must be proven before anything else. If unstable, everything above collapses into hallucinated structure or uncontrolled mutation.

provenance.originating_assertion: The minimal closure loop that proves the system is real

alternatives: No generative loop (static KG only) — rejected because it cannot self-heal
decisions.rationale: Without this closure loop, the system is a passive knowledge store, not a self-extending architecture. Every other decision derives from this one.
decisions.constraint_statement: Every CIR phantom MUST trigger a generative closure loop that resolves to a filesystem mutation and subsequent CIR confirmation. Any break in this chain is a system failure.
implications: Phase 1 wedge must implement this exact chain
CIR must be replay-safe to re-confirm phantoms after mutation

decisions.name: Topological Change Path
decisions.description: Realization-first path selected for primary topological change, with hybrid model per tier.

provenance.originating_assertion: Two architectural paths for topology change

alternatives: Proposal-first (phantom → proposal → review → promotion → reconciliation) — rejected: too slow, breaks closure
decisions.rationale: Realization-first (phantom → synthesis → staged write → reconciliation → rollback/commit) is faster and autonomous. Proposal-first retained for topology synthesis (deliberate evolution). Behavioral synthesis is human-reviewed last.
decisions.constraint_statement: Topology changes use proposal-first mode. Runtime binding uses staged realization. Behavioral synthesis is human-reviewed and deferred to Phase 2+.

decisions.name: Five Semantic Spaces
decisions.description: The system operates across five distinct semantic spaces: proposal, branch, staging, committed, validated.
alternatives: Two spaces (staging + committed only) — rejected: cannot support parallel exploration or branch history
decisions.rationale: Five spaces are required for the reconciliation loop to distinguish between candidate structure (proposal), parallel alternatives (branch), materialized-but-uncommitted (staging), authoritative (committed), and confirmed-correct (validated).
decisions.constraint_statement: Every persistent KG schema and pipeline stage MUST distinguish among the five spaces. Conflation of staging and committed is a design error.
implications: Q4 (versioning model) must support branch space
Projector must validate at staging→committed boundary

decisions.name: Reconciliation as Recursive Convergence
decisions.description: Reconciliation is not a validation pass — it is a recursive convergence loop: unresolved → generate → validate → enrich → regenerate.
alternatives: Validation-pass model (single pass, pass/fail) — rejected: cannot produce enriched context for regeneration
decisions.rationale: A single validation pass cannot feed back into synthesis with enriched context. Only a recursive loop can generate memory-bearing constraint satisfaction.
decisions.constraint_statement: Reconciliation MUST be a recursive convergence loop. It MUST produce reconciliation reports that feed back into topology synthesis. It MUST NOT be a single-pass validation gate.
implications: Reconciler must maintain state across iterations
Loop termination requires max_attempts and GENERATION_EXHAUSTED terminal state (dec-loop-termination)

decisions.name: Reconciliation Loop Termination
decisions.description: Loop termination governed by max_attempts per (artifact, category, target_path). GENERATION_EXHAUSTED is the terminal state for unconverged loops.

provenance.originating_assertion: Loop termination: max_attempts per (artifact, category, target_path), GENERATION_EXHAUSTED terminal state

alternatives: Infinite retry — rejected: uncontrolled, cannot surface failure
Timeout-based — rejected: not deterministic per artifact
decisions.rationale: Artifact-category-target_path key provides deterministic, traceable termination. GENERATION_EXHAUSTED is observable by CIR and governance.
decisions.constraint_statement: Reconciliation loops MUST terminate via max_attempts per (artifact, category, target_path). Unconverged loops MUST enter GENERATION_EXHAUSTED state, not silent retry.

decisions.name: Phase 1 Wedge Scope
decisions.description: Phase 1 is three components (CIR Generative Mode, Intent Packager, Safe FS Mutation) operating on topology artifacts only. No behavioral generation.
alternatives: Include behavioral generation in Phase 1 — rejected: too risky, cannot define correctness boundary yet
All 8 stages in Phase 1 — rejected: unbounded, cannot prove closure
decisions.constraint_statement: Phase 1 MUST NOT generate behavioral code. Only topology artifacts (files, directories, schemas, manifests, stubs). Behavioral generation is Phase 2+.
implications: Projector validates topology, not semantics
CIR phantoms are structural, not behavioral

decisions.name: Resolvable Existence Boundary
decisions.description: Behavioral generation ends at 'resolvable existence', not 'correct implementation.' The system generates compilable stubs, interface realizations, valid registrations, executable placeholders — but NOT correct business behavior, production logic, or safety-critical code.

provenance.originating_assertion: Behavioral generation stops at 'resolvable existence', not 'correct implementation'

alternatives: Generate correct behavior from the start — rejected: impossible without verification loop
No code generation at all — rejected: system cannot self-extend
decisions.constraint_statement: The projector MUST validate structural resolvability, not semantic correctness. Behavioral generation is limited to stubs, interface realizations, registrations, and executable placeholders.
implications: Qualifies what the KG needs to represent (topology, not behavior)
Projector is a structural validator, not a behavioral verifier

decisions.name: Mutation Model (Sandbox Filesystem)
decisions.description: All generative mutations write to a sandbox filesystem staging area, not in-memory proposals or direct production filesystem.

provenance.originating_assertion: Mutation model: sandbox filesystem (not in-memory proposals)

alternatives: In-memory proposals — rejected: not durable, no audit trail
Direct filesystem writes — rejected: no rollback boundary
decisions.rationale: Sandbox filesystem provides rollback boundary, audit trail, and staging→committed transition that the five-spaces model requires.
decisions.constraint_statement: All generative mutations MUST write to sandbox filesystem staging. No direct writes to committed space. The staging→committed transition requires projector validation.
implications: Safe FS Mutation component writes to staging only
Reconciler validates before promoting to committed

decisions.name: Module Placement (losm-generative)
decisions.description: losm-generative is the dedicated synthesis subsystem for self-extending architecture: topology synthesis, intent packaging, and safe filesystem mutation.

provenance.originating_assertion: Module placement: losm-generative as dedicated synthesis subsystem

alternatives: Splay across existing modules — rejected: cross-cutting concern, creates coupling
Standalone new module outside losm — rejected: loses losm's lifecycle governance
decisions.rationale: Placing generative synthesis inside losm gives it access to lifecycle state definitions and state semantics. Dedicated subsystem prevents coupling with existing execution logic.
decisions.constraint_statement: All self-extending synthesis code MUST reside in losm-generative. No generative logic in existing execution modules.

decisions.name: CIR Transport Format
decisions.description: CIR events use JSON Lines via stdout/stdin. stdout → file ingestion. No IPC yet.

provenance.originating_assertion: CIR transport: JSON Lines via stdout/stdin

alternatives: gRPC — rejected: overengineered for Phase 1
Unix sockets — rejected: adds coupling
HTTP — rejected: requires server
decisions.rationale: JSON Lines via stdout/stdin is the simplest possible transport. File ingestion from stdout enables replay and audit without IPC complexity.
decisions.constraint_statement: CIR generative events MUST use JSON Lines via stdout/stdin. No IPC in Phase 1.
implications: Every CIR generative event must be serializable to one JSON Line
File ingestion path must be idempotent (dec-idempotency)

decisions.name: CIR Generative Event Idempotency
decisions.description: Every CIR generative event must be replay-safe. Re-running the same CIR event must produce the same result or be safely no-oped.

provenance.originating_assertion: Idempotency: Every CIR generative event must be replay-safe

alternatives: Non-idempotent events — rejected: replay would produce duplicate mutations
decisions.rationale: Without idempotency, recovery from partial failure is impossible. Replay in the generative pipeline must be safe by design.
decisions.constraint_statement: Every CIR generative event MUST be idempotent. Replaying the same event MUST produce the same result or safely no-op.
implications: Event deduplication required at ingestion point
Mutation operations must be check-then-act

decisions.name: Phase 2+ Expansion Order
decisions.description: Post-wedge expansion order: Reconciliation → BranchManager → Proposal/Commit split → Runtime Synthesis → Behavior Synthesis (last).

provenance.originating_assertion: Expansion order: Reconciliation → BranchManager → Proposal/Commit split → Runtime Synthesis → Behavior Synthesis (last)

alternatives: Parallel expansion — rejected: dependencies between stages make parallel implementation inefficient
Behavior first — rejected: too risky without governance foundation
decisions.rationale: Reconciler must exist before BranchManager (reconciliation feeds branch scoring). BranchManager before Proposal/Commit split (branches inform split design). Runtime before behavior (must have resolvable existence before correct implementation).
decisions.constraint_statement: Post-wedge expansion MUST follow the order: Reconciliation → BranchManager → Proposal/Commit split → Runtime Synthesis → Behavior Synthesis (last).

decisions.name: Provenance Causal Chain Requirement
decisions.description: Every artifact must carry a complete causal chain: Artifact ← generated_from ← reconciliation_of ← branch_selected_by ← synthesized_from ← CIR_event ← originating_assertion.

provenance.originating_assertion: Provenance Graph Layer: full causal chain

alternatives: Single-step provenance (artifact → source only) — rejected: cannot support rollback or governance traceability
decisions.rationale: Because the system mutates itself, single-step provenance is insufficient. Rollback, governance, and topology drift analysis all require the full causal chain from originating assertion through each reconciliation iteration.
decisions.constraint_statement: Every artifact in the system MUST trace to its originating assertion through the full causal chain. Any artifact without complete provenance is opaque and MUST be treated as untrusted.
implications: Extends ASSERTED/INFERRED/DERIVED provenance labels (Section 29.6) to full graph ancestry
Reconciler must annotate reconciliation reports with causal chain links

decisions.name: Losing Branches as Learning Data
decisions.description: Non-selected synthesis branches must be preserved as evolutionary architectural memory, not discarded.
alternatives: Discard losing branches — rejected: loses learning data, governance history, and synthesis priors
decisions.rationale: Losing branches contain topology learning data (which strategies converge fastest), governance history (which violate constraints most), synthesis priors (which generate minimal diffs), and architectural lineage (high-risk artifact classes). Discarding them loses evolutionary memory.
decisions.constraint_statement: BranchManager MUST archive non-selected branches. They MUST be queryable by CIR, reconciliation, and governance. Deletion is prohibited.
implications: Q4 (versioning model) must be event-logged — latest-only cannot preserve branch history
BranchManager must distinguish active from archived branches

decisions.name: TypeSpec as Contract Surface (JVM mirror)
decisions.description: TypeSpec is the contract surface that mirrors the JVM enforcement layer. TypeSpec = contract surface, JVM = enforcement boundary. Invalid transitions fail at compile time (TypeSpec → OpenAPI → Java types). Conduit exposes only WorkRequest at the HTTP boundary — Observation/Projection/IR/SynthesizedView cannot be represented in the API schema.

provenance.originating_assertion: TypeSpec = contract surface. JVM = enforcement boundary. No runtime 'CIRS engine'. Instead: invalid flows fail at compile time (TypeSpec → OpenAPI → Java types).

alternatives: Runtime CIRS validation engine — rejected: adds runtime overhead, cannot prevent invalid transitions at compile time
No contract surface — rejected: transitions would be documented but not enforced
decisions.rationale: TypeSpec generates OpenAPI, which generates Java types at compile time. This means illegal transitions (IR → Conduit, Projection → Execution) are unrepresentable — they don't exist in the schema, cannot be serialized, cannot be sent. The JVM boundary is the enforcement layer, not a runtime system.
decisions.constraint_statement: TypeSpec MUST be the contract surface for all cross-boundary transitions. The Conduit HTTP gateway MUST only expose WorkRequest. Observation, Projection, ProjectionIR, and SynthesizedView MUST NOT appear in any Conduit-facing API schema. Invalid transitions MUST fail at compile time, not runtime.
implications: The TypeSpec model mirrors the JVM enforcement layer — they are isomorphic
CIRS enforcement happens at compile time through TypeSpec → OpenAPI → Java, not at runtime

decisions.name: KG as Writable Projection (not read-only artifact)
decisions.description: The KG is the semantic graph. The filesystem (and PostgreSQL) are writable projections of it. The generative pipeline resolves CIR phantoms by mutating the KG's projections into operational reality.

provenance.originating_assertion: The filesystem becomes a writable projection of a semantic graph, not a static repository

alternatives: KG as read-only snapshot — rejected: cannot drive self-extending topology changes
decisions.rationale: A read-only KG can describe phantoms but cannot resolve them. The KG must be a writable projection to close the generative loop: CIR detects phantom → KG drives synthesis → filesystem mutation → CIR confirms resolution → KG updated.
decisions.constraint_statement: The KG MUST be a writable projection surface for topology synthesis. Filesystem and PostgreSQL mutations are projections of KG state. Read-only KG is incompatible with the self-extending architecture.
implications: Supersedes the read-only KG assumption from earlier architecture (Section 11)
Projector must validate mutations before committing to KG

gaps_and_blockers.description: Canonicalizer / Commit Layer does not exist. Prerequisite for Atten to be actionable.
XIL (External Intelligence Layer) does not exist. Without XIL, external inputs would enter GEL directly, violating the invariant that canonical state is always clean.
No bridge exists between JVM/Spring operator plane and the WRP pipeline. They are two independent stacks.
Nebula discovers and structures markdown. The conduit pipeline never consumes it. No bridge exists.
Pipeline is blocked: .api-blocked file present in .conduit-data/.
ProjectionIR is spec-only. Needs: schema definition, 6 adapter implementations, synthesis prototype, CIRS-IR validation checks, integration wiring.
PEB Spring Boot Phase 1 (kernel skeleton) is the planned next implementation phase but has not started.

Transform type evolution (v0-v4) is spec-only. Actual conduit runtime uses simpler, untyped execution model with no StateView/StateDelta separation, no Context validation of transforms, and no structured Trace as first-class output.
Context is still treated as spatial container or memory context, not as a behavioral rule-set over state with invariants, allowedTransforms, and execution mode.
HarnessDefinition (3-level data-driven tool wrapper: store enums -> store templates -> store semantic translators) is not implemented. Conduit still uses hardcoded tool wrappers.
ExecutionMode (ONESHOT/INTERACTIVE/DAEMON) differentiation is not implemented in conduit. All executions treated as ONESHOT.
RoleMappingStrategy (AGENT/PROMPT_FILE/SYSTEM_FLAG) is not implemented in harness. Role injection is hardcoded.

XIL admission gates (TTS=Truthfulness, STOA=Scope/Type/Origin Authority, TSP=Time/Space/Presence, PEL=Projection Envelope Limit) are entirely spec-only. No validation gates exist in current intake pipeline.
Authority Arbitration Layer (sits between Envelope -> CEI) with ContextScope tokens and weight-based authority domains is concept-only. Global ontology bias freely overpowers local execution scoping.
Event vs Incident type distinction (event=factual immutable, incident=typed actionable subset with state machine) is not reflected in any DB schema or pipeline routing.
gaps_and_blockers.source: Event System Design.html, Bug Tracking Architecture.html

gaps_and_blockers.description: 2-tier compiler model (Pro=Governor for planning/synthesis, Flash=WorkerSwarm for execution/retrieval/tool use) is concept-only. No compiled execution graph exists.

PersistenceTriad principle (only Canonical Spec + Decision Log + ExecutionReceipt should persist) is not adopted. Many more than 3 things persist in the current system (session state, intermediate artifacts, etc.).
External Agent Model with TrustScore (dynamic weighting, not binary trust) is concept-only. No external signal governance exists.
Reality Constraint Layer with Reality Projection Function, drift detection (external vs internal), and 4 signal categories is concept-only. No feedback loop from real-world outcomes.
MIGL (Model Internal Governance Layer) for governing model-level reasoning constraints is concept-only. No internal reasoning governance exists.

CapabilityOperator model (single-purpose, composable, swappable, independently testable operator selected by type-driven matching) is not implemented. Tools are still invoked as programs, not as capability operators.
TypedWorkflowGraph (typed process graph over Atten with domain patterns for software/research/business/systems) is concept-only. No workflow graph infrastructure exists.
Dual-agent design review pattern (Kiro/architecture-first vs DeepSeek/implementation-aware as concurrent review mechanism) is not established. AI agents do not participate in architecture review.
Observation as evidentiary record (interpretive) vs Event as factual record is not reflected in DB schema or pipeline. Observer produces raw data without separating observation from fact.

PostgreSQL + pgvector schema for the persistent knowledge graph does not exist. Table-per-type model, provenance columns (ASSERTED/INFERRED/DERIVED/TEMPORAL_SCOPE), embedding columns, and foreign keys are all undesigned. Constrained by Layer A resolution (Q1+Q3).

The incremental merge model (persist(KGₙ₋₁) + merge(deltas)) is concept-only. No delta extraction logic, no merge algorithm, no conflict resolution, no projector validation on merge exist. Merge algorithm depends on Q1 resolution (unit of update).

Provenance labels (ASSERTED/INFERRED/DERIVED/TEMPORAL_SCOPE) are not applied to any knowledge graph data. Every node/edge in nexus-knowledge-graph.json is unlabeled — all data is implicitly ASSERTED, including inferred relationships. Resolution in Layer A (Q8 — source anchoring).

The projector (formal constraint function) does not exist in any form. No DDL-level constraints beyond basic type checking. No application-level validation pass. No embedding projection. No normative projector governing BP output. This is Q3 — the trust boundary decision. Pending Q1+Q3 joint resolution.

pgvector embedding generation pipeline is undesigned. What gets embedded (node descriptions? relationship semantics? transcript chunks?), when (sync on write? async background job?), and how stale embeddings are detected all derivable from Q1+Q3 resolution (Layer B).

The 3-tier graph model (Spec Graph / Inference Graph / Execution Graph) is not wired into any pipeline. Current architecture conflates all three tiers into a single nexus-knowledge-graph.json file with no tier separation. Resolution depends on Layer A+B+C completion.
Agent read path for the persistent KG is undesigned. No SQL direct access, no REST API, no MCP tool, no query interface. This is Q5 — the cognition interface decision. Derivative of Q1+Q3 resolution.

The KG shares a PostgreSQL instance with PEB state. Cross-store consistency guarantees between KG tables and PEB tables are undefined. This is Q7 — the memory partitioning problem. Derivative of Layer A+B resolution.

Versioning model for the persistent KG is undecided between latest-only (no history), event-logged (full history), or snapshot-versioned (checkpoint model). This is Q4 — temporal semantics of truth. Derivative of Q1 resolution (granularity determines log size).

The Phase 1 wedge (CIR Generative Mode + Intent Packager + Safe FS Mutation) does not exist. No phantom detection, no event→WorkRequest conversion, no staging sandbox for scaffold topology writes. The core claim (CIR phantom → generative event → filesystem mutation → CIR resolution) is unproven.

LOSM-Generative as dedicated synthesis subsystem (module placement from Self-Extending Architecture) does not exist. No dedicated location for topology synthesis, intent packaging, or safe FS mutation code.

Reconciler (recursive convergence loop — unresolved → generate → validate → enrich → regenerate) does not exist. No iterative constraint satisfaction loop. No reconciliation report feedback into topology synthesis.
BranchManager (parallel synthesis branches, candidate scoring, losing branch preservation) does not exist. No branch scoring, no branch history, no evolutionary selection of synthesis candidates.

Provenance causal chain (Artifact ← generated_from ← reconciliation_of ← branch_selected_by ← synthesized_from ← CIR_event ← originating_assertion) does not exist. No artifact carries full provenance ancestry. Rollback is impossible. Topology drift is opaque.

The five spaces of self-extension (proposal/branch/staging/committed/validated) are not modeled in any schema or pipeline. The current system conflates staging and committed. Branch space does not exist.
CIR generative event idempotency is not guaranteed. No replay-safe event mechanism. No event deduplication for phantom detection.
Generative pipeline loop termination is not implemented. No max_attempts per (artifact, category, target_path), no GENERATION_EXHAUSTED terminal state. Generative loops could run indefinitely.
